pending_qa.q: What is the role of artificial intelligence in modern construction surveying and project delivery?
pending_qa.r: AI is a massively successful tool for research, design access statement reports, and feasibilities when you can easily pull up planning applications around a site using AI and ChatGPT to help inform and speed up the process of getting to a solution. However, AI will never take away the core reason someone wants to work with you—it won't be because you have an AI tool they don't.

pending_qa.q: Why is mentorship and proximity between senior and junior staff critical in construction consultancies?
pending_qa.r: Early career individuals need to be absolutely around seniors who will teach them—the way you learn, the way everybody learns. Leaders overhear things happening in the office and can course-correct, and those things just don't happen when working remotely. No one's going to send you a Teams message every 10 minutes; you need to be present.

pending_qa.q: What misconceptions exist about whether young professionals should pursue quantity surveying as a career?
pending_qa.r: Most young people are money motivated or looking for stable careers. Unless they have a real passion for construction sites and are fairly savvy with numbers, they should probably lead into more technically focused roles like site engineer or project manager. There are more appetizing avenues to make a living, which is probably why data shows we continue to struggle with fewer graduates coming through each year.

pending_qa.q: How should business leaders approach rapid decision-making versus prolonged analysis?
pending_qa.r: Make decisions quickly. If it doesn't work, you can always reverse. But if you're going to do something, give it everything and go for it. Nine times out of ten, if you give it conviction and you put some time, effort, and money into it, things move forward. Some businesses just die through indecision because they don't make a decision and get on with it.

pending_qa.q: What challenges do male employees face when requesting flexible working arrangements in construction?
pending_qa.r: When men try to work flexibly and put in their request to do it, it's perceived differently among their peers and from senior environments because it's almost like 'why do you need to?' The industry has been putting nuclear in metal tubes for 50 years and driving around the oceans, so the perception is suddenly putting it on a site in Wales is too risky, even though the technology has been proven.

pending_qa.q: How important is public awareness and education about what quantity surveyors actually do?
pending_qa.r: If you did a street poll and asked Joe Bloggs what a QS is, you'd probably get 70% saying 'don't really know.' At grassroots level coming through school, when you ask kids where they want to be when they grow up, none of them say QS, but it's actually a really great career—well paid and increasingly well paid with opportunities everywhere.

pending_qa.q: What structural approach helps construction firms balance client satisfaction with sustainable growth?
pending_qa.r: You need to reduce the workload of business owners in terms of project delivery to allow growth in other areas, while making sure clients remain 100% happy with the service they're getting. Over 50% of the business should be at director or project director level, with people who want more responsibility but won't overreach, as that balance is equally important.

pending_qa.q: What is the fundamental difference between technical expertise and business leadership in construction?
pending_qa.r: Learn your technical aspect first and be happy with what you're learning and growing. You can't be the general unless you've been the soldier—unless you know what's happening, how can you tell others what to do? Then learn how to manage people, which has its own challenges and rewards. Finally, when you're ready, run a business and be prepared for the good, bad, and indifferent.

pending_qa.q: How should quantity surveyors advise clients on project costs beyond lowest-cost tendering?
pending_qa.r: As a QS, your job is to know what the price of a project is—the build cost. It's not just about finding the lowest tender. You might be buying a problem; we've seen contractors bid too low and go out of business. Use AI to make yourself more efficient and produce better data to analyse and give opinions on, but never replace the judgment that comes from experience.
